stability: MCP tool names and input schemas are additive: existing names never change meaning, and new capability arrives as new tools. Repository routes are named by method and path; a route that moves or is removed breaks every agent written against this contract. The repository MCP tools are opt-in: they are always LISTED so the contract stays stable, but they answer 'not configured' and make no network call unless MW_MCP_SERVICE_URL and MW_MCP_TOKEN are both set.

tools.name: okf.validate
tools.summary: Validate an OKF document supplied in the request and return the validation report (document-level; no repository, no network)

tools.name: graph.stats
tools.summary: Graph health of an OKF document supplied in the request: nodes, edges, isolated nodes, components (document-level; no repository, no network)

tools.name: gate.run
tools.summary: Run the round-trip fidelity gate between two OKF documents supplied in the request and return its evidence record (document-level; no repository, no network)

tools.name: okf.diff
tools.summary: Semantic diff between two OKF documents supplied in the request: elements, edges and attributes (document-level; no repository, no network)

tools.name: repo.projects
tools.summary: List the projects the configured token may see. Repository mode (opt-in): requires MW_MCP_SERVICE_URL and MW_MCP_TOKEN; read permission.

tools.name: repo.branches
tools.summary: List a project's branches and their tips. Repository mode (opt-in): read permission.

tools.name: repo.commits
tools.summary: List the commits on a project's branch (default main). Repository mode (opt-in): read permission.

tools.name: repo.read
tools.summary: Read the OKF model behind a commit and its commit record (provenance). Repository mode (opt-in): read permission.

tools.name: repo.find
tools.summary: Search a revision's elements by name, id or stereotype fragment, returning each match's id, name and kind. Repository mode (opt-in): read permission.

tools.name: repo.element
tools.summary: Read one element by id from a revision: its attributes and its graph edges. Repository mode (opt-in): read permission.

tools.name: repo.coverage
tools.summary: Requirement coverage for a revision: covered and uncovered, each named, from the engine's requirement_coverage. Repository mode (opt-in): read permission.

tools.name: repo.references
tools.summary: A model's typed subsystem references, with an optional resolve flag for each reference's resolve state (the same resolution the UI and API use). Repository mode (opt-in): read permission.

tools.name: repo.importReport
tools.summary: Read a migration's loss report and the engine's fidelity measurement, by retained artifact hash. Repository mode (opt-in): read permission.

tools.name: repo.lossSummary
tools.summary: A migration's loss report aggregated by construct and verdict with counts, plus paging over the full list. Repository mode (opt-in): read permission.

tools.name: repo.artifact
tools.summary: The retained original bytes of a migrated artifact, byte for byte. Repository mode (opt-in): read permission.

tools.name: repo.diff
tools.summary: Diff two commits and run the round-trip gate LOCALLY from the two models read from the repository, returning the verdict and the evidence; never records a run (recording is a write). Repository mode (opt-in): read permission.

tools.name: repo.audit
tools.summary: Read a project's append-only audit log. Repository mode (opt-in): read permission.

tools.name: repo.checks
tools.summary: Read the gate checks recorded against a commit (what has been checked about this model). Repository mode (opt-in): review permission.

tools.name: repo.proposals
tools.summary: The project's proposals with their decisions and who made them. Repository mode (opt-in): read permission.

tools.name: repo.analytics
tools.summary: The portfolio question: which models meet which requirements, read from the project analytics route. Repository mode (opt-in): read permission.

tools.name: repo.propose
tools.summary: Record a proposal for a human to review and decide. The agent's output: it persists a proposal (review permission) and never writes a change - a human accepts it. Repository mode (opt-in).

repositoryHttpSurface.auth: Every endpoint except /health and /version requires the same authentication a human meets and enforces the listed permission plus project scope: an unauthenticated caller is refused 401, an under-privileged caller 403. There is no agent-only path.

repositoryMode.notes: Repository mode is enabled only when BOTH MW_MCP_SERVICE_URL (the running service's base URL, plain http) and MW_MCP_TOKEN (the bearer token) are set. With neither set the MCP server is a pure document processor that makes no network call; the repository tools are listed but answer 'not configured'. The tools reach the running service over the same HTTP surface a human uses, authenticated with the token, and issue only read (GET) routes plus the single propose route (POST /projects/:project/proposals, review permission). No tool calls a write route; a write attempt is refused by the service with 403 and surfaced as a clear tool error, never a crash or a retry.

agentContract.agentIsAClient: An agent may read and propose; it may not write. An agent token cannot hold a write or admin role, and every write route refuses an agent with 403. There is no privileged agent path; a human performs changes through the ordinary routes.
agentContract.documentLevel: The first four MCP tools operate on documents supplied in the request and never touch a repository.
agentContract.repositoryLevel: The repo.* MCP tools are opt-in read-and-propose tools over the running service; they are inert (and network-free) unless MW_MCP_SERVICE_URL and MW_MCP_TOKEN are both set, and they never call a write route.
agentContract.audit: Every write is recorded in the audit log with the actor (the verified subject), the mechanism (open, static, jwt or agent) and, for agents, the authorizer the agent acted for.
